title: Return browser-ready compatibility output from document reads
decision: SG-0013 document-read endpoints should return browser-ready rendered compatibility output from the local service, along with sanitized document metadata, stable anchor data, source/compliance orientation, and artifact placeholder/context data. React should own the shell, navigation, selected-document state, filtering, and reader controls, but should not be forced to rebuild the old Markdown/CFR/compliance renderer from raw Markdown in this slice.
context: The renderer strategy is already to use live compatibility rendering before polished React renderer rebuilds. SG-0013 now needs a concrete service contract for document reads so the full EPP browser can show real documents quickly without turning the first browser-shell slice into a full renderer rewrite.
rationale: Returning reader-ready compatibility output from the service restores browseability for policies, Appendix A, Survey Guidance, CFR, and artifact-heavy documents while preserving the later path to native React renderers for high-value surfaces.
alternatives_considered: Return only raw Markdown plus metadata and have React render everything in SG-0013
Pre-render the full corpus as static browser output during import
Delay full document readability until SG-0014
consequences: The document-read endpoint should render from current canonical source at request time rather than serving a static pre-rendered corpus
The normal reader payload should include compatibility-rendered content and enough metadata for anchors, source/compliance orientation, and artifact placeholders
React should consume the rendered payload for normal browsing and keep UI state/presentation concerns in the app
Raw Markdown may remain available later for editor/debug workflows, but SG-0013 should not depend on raw Markdown as the primary reader payload
SG-0014 can deepen renderer, editing, and proposal-review parity on top of the SG-0013 compatibility reader path
